title: Function extensionality for σ_invol (Putnam 2025 A3), split at the first nonzero coordinate
intent: Prove that the strategy map σ is an involution (σ (σ x) = x) by function extensionality: ext i reduces the function equality to a pointwise goal at an arbitrary coordinate, by_cases on i = firstNonzero x hx splits it into the coordinate σ touches and all others, and each branch closes with σ's two pointwise rewrite lemmas plus the involution of swap12.

parent.name: σ_invol
parent.statement: lemma σ_invol {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → Fin 3) (hx : x ≠ fun _ => 0) : σ (σ x hx) (σ_ne_zero x hx) = x

children.name: at_firstNonzero
children.statement: pointwise goal at coordinate `firstNonzero x hx`, after ext i, by_cases hi : i = firstNonzero x hx and subst hi: (σ (σ x hx) (σ_ne_zero x hx)) (firstNonzero x hx) = x (firstNonzero x hx)
children.closed_by: rw [eq1, eq2, swap12_invol], where eq1 unfolds the outer σ at that coordinate (conv_lhs => rw [σ, if_pos hk_σ.symm]) and eq2 is σ_at_firstNonzero x hx

children.name: away_firstNonzero
children.statement: pointwise goal at coordinate `i` under hi : i ≠ firstNonzero x hx: (σ (σ x hx) (σ_ne_zero x hx)) i = x i
children.closed_by: rw [eq1, eq2], where eq1 unfolds the outer σ away from that coordinate (conv_lhs => rw [σ, if_neg (by rwa [hk_σ])]) and eq2 is σ_away_firstNonzero x hx i hi

applicability.goal_shape: an equality of functions f = g where f is defined pointwise by an `if i = p then … else …` whose test is a single canonical point p of the domain (here σ, which touches only `firstNonzero x`); the move turns it into ∀ i, f i = g i and then splits on i = p.
applicability.use_when: the equality is between functions (so ext i applies), the function differs from the identity only at one identifiable coordinate, and the pointwise rewrite lemmas for 'at p' and 'away from p' are already stated; the canonical point must be preserved by the map (firstNonzero_σ) so the outer and inner occurrences align.
applicability.avoid_when: the canonical point p is not invariant under the map (then the by_cases/subst will not typecheck); the two regions need genuinely different arguments beyond the function's definitional rewrites; or the equality is not between functions but between data the extensionality tactic cannot decompose.

claims.claim: The parent σ_invol is closed by its two children: ext i turns the function equality into a pointwise goal, by_cases hi : i = firstNonzero x hx yields the two branches, and each branch closes with a single rw (line 106 `rw [eq1, eq2, swap12_invol]`; line 110 `rw [eq1, eq2]`), leaving no remaining goals.

claims.claim: The authors state the structural fact that makes the split work, as a comment: 'Key insight: σ only modifies the first nonzero position' (above σ_inj).
σ_invol is reused later in the same file to prove injectivity of σ: `have h1 := σ_invol x hx` and `have h2 := σ_invol y hy` (lines 127-128), and again `rw [key, σ_invol]` at line 560.

The proof of σ_invol is 16 lines total (95-110); the extensionality step ext i and the split by_cases are 2 lines (97 and 99), and each of the two branches is closed by one rw (lines 106 and 110). The two rewrite lemmas σ_at_firstNonzero and σ_away_firstNonzero are one-line proofs (lines 72 and 76).

metrics.how_counted: lines 95-110 of the copied file; children = the two goals created by by_cases hi : i = firstNonzero x hx; helper lemmas used in the proof: firstNonzero_σ (for hk_σ), σ_at_firstNonzero, σ_away_firstNonzero, swap12_invol

consequences: ext i reduces a function equality to a pointwise goal over an arbitrary i, and by_cases hi : i = firstNonzero x hx then demands that both regions are covered. The split only aligns because firstNonzero is invariant under σ (firstNonzero_σ, bound as hk_σ): without it the two σ occurrences in σ (σ x hx) would unfold at different coordinates and the rewrites would not close. Each branch must supply its own unfolding of σ (conv_lhs => rw [σ, if_pos/if_neg]); if the if-condition is not decidable, by_cases cannot split the goal at all.
